subject.title: [Bug]: Deep-profile release gate treats instrumented RSS as baseline-eligible

question: Should maintainers accept the profiled-resource-only Kova DO_NOT_SHIP tolerance proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102894, or handle profiler overhead through Kova thresholds/profile policy instead?
rationale: The source-backed bug is clear, but the fix deliberately changes release-gate automation behavior and the protected maintainer-owned issue already has a draft PR for that decision.

options.title: Review The Linked PR
options.body: Accept the narrow adapter direction only after the PR is ready and exact-head proof covers the real retry report plus negative gate cases.

options.title: Move The Policy To Kova
options.body: Keep OpenClaw strict and change Kova's release profile, thresholds, or profiling classification upstream instead.

options.title: Keep DO_NOT_SHIP Strict
options.body: Leave all Kova DO_NOT_SHIP verdicts blocking and require release operators to rerun without deep profiling for baseline-eligible decisions.

recommendation.title: Review The Linked PR
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow adapter direction only after the PR is ready and exact-head proof covers the real retry report plus negative gate cases.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the issue, the linked fix PR, and the pinned Kova profiling contract referenced by the report.
